body.statement: At each fixed \(P\in\mathcal P_L\) with \(p_{dj}>0\) for every \((d,j)\in\mathcal D\times\mathcal Y_L\), suppose that one affine certificate contrast is uniquely active for a specified scalar endpoint, is separated by a positive gap from every competing contrast, and has positive asymptotic variance.  Is the corresponding scalar side of the finite-sample honest procedure in \(\text{thm:finite-sample-support-honesty}\) asymptotically equivalent to the semiparametrically efficient Wald interval?  The answer must specify whether the limiting critical value uses the global level \(\alpha\) or the procedure's simultaneous error allocation and must preserve the stated simultaneous coverage guarantee.
body.justification: Identification without boundary-valid uncertainty quantification is inadequate for sparse multi-arm ordinal trials.
body.gap: ChoRussell2024 perturbs LPs for uniform validity and FangSantos2019 simulates directional derivatives; neither delivers finite-sample support honesty plus pointwise efficient scalar adaptation for this six-endpoint map.
body.consumer: The result supplies a single prespecified report that remains honest in small trial cells without paying a permanent efficiency penalty on regular faces.

obligation.what_is_open: Prove a uniform local conditional-multinomial normal and quantile approximation over the shrinking random pilot region, then invert it and identify the correct global or simultaneous critical value for the regular scalar side.
obligation.obstruction: Exact least-favourable inversion gives finite-sample honesty, but pointwise multinomial asymptotic normality alone does not control the nuisance supremum or its quantile uniformly on the pilot region. A global level alpha critical value and a Bonferroni-allocated critical value are different first-order intervals.
obligation.attempted: The finite exact construction was completed and the affine endpoint map was shown globally Lipschitz with a root-\(N\) plug-in rate. These results control estimation error but do not establish the \(o_P(N^{-1/2})\) quantile and endpoint-inversion remainder required for interval equivalence.
obligation.partial_result: The emitted theorem \(\text{thm:finite-sample-support-honesty}\) proves exact simultaneous coverage for every \(N\), including empty arms, zero cells, and tied facets, by pilot-region error control and least-favourable conditional product-multinomial inversion.  The emitted theorem \(\text{thm:fixed-l-endpoint-lipschitz-rate}\) separately proves the fixed-\(L\) plug-in rate \(O_P((N\pi_{\min})^{-1/2})\).  Neither result proves that the random least-favourable inversion quantile, after pilot localization and simultaneous allocation, differs by \(o_P(N^{-1/2})\) from a specified efficient Wald critical value.
